### "Briefly discuss how much accuracy the student retains compared to the teacher"
#### Teacher Model
To document the evaluation of the student model compared to the teacher model, I want to discuss the models themselves. With the teacher model, I decided to use Google's Bert transformer. Seeing the warning that shows up about the model needing to be trained, one thing I can hypothesize from this is that the teacher model simply needed to be trained more. The metrics back it up - as upon evaluation, looking at our accuracy and confusion matrix, the model only predicts negative cases (both true negatives and false negatives). Recall and F1 scores of 0 further back this up. 

Another reason I believe the model needs to be trained more is because upon evaluating the label balance within the dataset upon splitting into training, validation, and testing, there was an even number of both labels in each set. If we had somewhat of a class imbalance (maybe a 60-40 or 70-30 ratio of either label), then we could have made the assumption that the label is overfitting to the majority class. However, given the very even split, this shows there was no overfitting to a majority class, rather the model not being trained enough to tune the weights and biases for the Bert model - further proving the teacher model was not trained on enough epochs.

Looking at the teacher model's AUCs, we can see that the AUROC = 0.57 and the AUPRC = 0.55. Given what we have already hypothesized about the model having not trained enough, the AUCs of the teacher model provide evidence that the hypothesis is true. The AUROC indicates the model is learning (though slightly). If we had achieved an AUROC of 0.5, then we could conclude that the model is either randomly guessing or just picking the majority class. Since our AUROC > 0.5, again at 0.57, we can conclude the model did learn a bit in the one epoch, however not enough training was done for the model to continue learning and classify better.

#### Student Model
For the student model, I decided to use a smaller, fine-tuned model as our student model for the distillation portion of this. This is my first time incorporating knowledge distillation using pre-trained models, so I had a lot to try, experiment, and learn from! Going off the teacher model's performance, we can see that the student model did indeed learn from the teacher model, and if not, a lot more. We can determine this by looking at the metrics.

Looking at the accuracy and confusion matrix, we can see the model's ability to not overfit to one class is substantially better than the teacher model, with the confusion matrix showing strong diagonal performance, around 10000 true negatives predicted and just over 9000 true positives predicted with around 3000 false negatives and slightly less than 2000 false positives. This performance is strong, indicating the model is not overfitting to the data, as we would prefer for the model to not overfit to the training data and be able to generalize better. However, there is still a lot that can be done to fine-tune the model for even better performance to reduce both the false positives and false negatives.

Interpretting the AUCs of the student model, we have much better AUCs with an AUROC and AUPRC of 0.89. AN AUROC of 0.89 indicates the model is performing very strongly (and could be a better metric for model performance than accuracy alone). The AUROC of the model indicates that the model is able to strongly predict either class - showing signs of neither underfitting or overfitting. AUPRC of 0.89 implies that the model has a strong performance against sensitivity - which wasn't a problem we had to begin with, but showing the ability to be able to distinguish between true and false cases shows a ton of improvement from the model via distillation. 

A precision and recall score of 0.84 and 0.73 shows the models ability to generalize well to the labels, both telling of the amount of false positives and false negatives shown in the confusion matrix. In conclusion, this shows the student models ability to generalize the dataset well enough without the possibility of overfitting to the dataset.
